actions.mechanism: Round-robin nonempty customer queues, granting one dispatch per turn regardless of estimated runtime.
actions.implementation: Maintain a rotating customer cursor; append newly active customers behind existing waiters. Dispatch immediately whenever any of the twelve workers becomes free.
actions.check: With at most N active customers, verify each continuously queued customer starts work within 60N seconds. Measure mean latency separately; this bounds dispatch fairness.
actions.risk: Equal dispatch opportunities do not imply equal worker-time shares.

actions.action: Alternate short-job preference with oldest-job protection
actions.mechanism: Within each customer's turn, select estimated-shortest jobs three times, then the oldest waiting job once.
actions.implementation: Store a per-customer modulo-four dispatch counter. Preserve arrival order for oldest-job selection; inaccurate estimates never remove the protected oldest-job opportunity.
actions.check: Test continuous heavy arrivals, occasional short jobs, and reversed runtime estimates. Verify every fourth customer dispatch selects oldest; a job with k predecessors needs at most 4(k+1) customer turns.
actions.risk: Misclassification can worsen mean latency, but cannot eliminate oldest-job progress.

actions.action: Alternatively, reserve one worker for guaranteed progress
actions.mechanism: Separate fairness from latency optimization: one worker rotates customers; eleven prefer globally estimated-shortest jobs.
actions.implementation: Replace the preceding dispatch policy with this split. The fairness worker takes each customer's oldest job; all workers share atomic queue removal.
actions.check: Under continuous sixty-second submissions and short arrivals with inverted estimates, verify customer start gaps stay within 60N seconds for at most N active customers; report mean latency independently.
actions.risk: The fairness worker cannot accelerate short jobs already blocked behind running transforms.
